description:
DONE s460ao (agent AO, round 17).  Fixed by direction (c), the runtime
decline — NOT (a) or (b), and the reason is worth keeping.

WHY NOT THE CLASSIFIER.  (a) "veto a method-call initializer" only covers one
spelling: the B-regime fires precisely when the write shape is UNPROVEN, so an
overloaded object can arrive from a hash element, a sub return, a global, or a
string eval just as easily as from `->new`.  (b) "widen the scan to the modules
the file loads" is incomplete for the same reason (an object can come from a
module the file never names) AND it is the more expensive de-optimization: it
would kill the raw slot for EVERY numeric lexical in any file that touches an
overload-carrying module, where the decline costs only the values that actually
carry handlers.  Both were weighed and rejected on those grounds, not on
effort.

WHAT SHIPPED (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp only — emission byte-identical, no
generation bump, no artifact regeneration):

1. `%pcl-raw-coerce-check` (die) -> `%pcl-raw-freeze-unsafe-p` (predicate).
   `%pcl-to-number-strict` / `%pcl-to-string-strict` now store
   **`(p-box-init V)`** when it answers true: a fresh box under box-set's own
   assignment rules, i.e. EXACTLY what the general-form compiler would have
   stored for that write.  The slot then holds the general form's own
   representation, and since every raw-slot consumer is polymorphic (`setf`,
   the `-raw` twins, `prog1`, reads through ordinary `p-*` ops), the optimized
   emission runs identically to PCL_OPT=none BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by a
   case analysis of consumers.  ir-spec §2.2 amended (this is the one
   exception to "a raw slot never holds a box").

2. THE PREDICATE IS "ANY OPERATOR", NOT `""`/`0+` — and that half was a
   SILENT WRONG the die never caught.  A class overloading `<=>` alone gets
   every numeric comparison autogenerated from it; the frozen slot compared
   the ref's stable ID, so `CmpOnly->new(42) > 10` answered 0 where perl
   answers 1 (probed both ways; `PCL_NO_RAW_VERDICT=1` was right).  ONE
   reading now, `%p-class-overloaded-p`, shared with `overload::Overloaded`
   (`p-overloaded`) — which ALSO gained the @ISA walk it was missing, because
   perl's own overload::Overloaded answers true for a subclass of an
   overloaded parent (probed 5.40.3).

3. `perl-increment` unboxed BEFORE numifying, throwing the class away so
   to-number could never dispatch `0+`.  That made ONE program give TWO
   answers once values started surviving the write (`$o++;$o++;print $o+0`:
   3 under PCL_OPT=none, 7 by default).  It now asks the BOX.  The residue —
   perl AUTOGENERATES `++` from a `+` handler and keeps an OBJECT — is
   PRE-EXISTING on both paths and filed as **#900**.

BENCH (tools/bench-exec.pl, same machine, before -> after):
  intloop+= 0.0188 -> 0.0186 | intloop= 0.0179 -> 0.0177 | cfor 0.0252 ->
  0.0258 | feread 0.1855 -> 0.1859 | arrhash 0.0821 -> 0.0840 | strcat
  0.0033 -> 0.0030 | ovlsub 0.1306 -> 0.1320   (all within noise)
  **collatz 0.7704 -> 0.4859 s, 0.40x -> 0.25x perl** (best-of-5 confirmed
  0.4863).  Not luck: collatz has two B-regime writes per iteration, and the
  old check asked `p-find-overload` TWICE out-of-line plus %pcl-dualvar-p on
  a RAW number.  The predicate now settles a raw operand on ONE inline
  p-box-p test.  This is the DECIDED.md s458ak note ("%pcl-raw-coerce-check
  asks the predicate twice per iteration on a RAW number") paid off.

BAR MET: 14-probe battery vs perl 5.40.3, each probe run under perl / PCL
default / PCL_OPT=none — 13 agree in all three, the 14th is #900 with raw and
general now agreeing.  The two headline probes were verified to FAIL before
the change (the #890 die; `gt10:0` for the <=>-only class).  Gate PASS
191/6434 on a fresh core (= s459f's xs-less 6427 + the 7 new guard rows).
Full sweep GATE clean, TOTAL passing 18340 (+0), drops 5 = census, 0 new /
0 fixed.  Guard: the `#890` block in Pl/t/raw-verdict-01.t (7 rows, incl. a
PCL_OPT=none equivalence row and the negatives that keep the decline from
widening — a plain blessed ref still freezes to its stable ID).

DOCS: docs/raw-numeric-verdict.md gains "Checked coercion — the runtime
DECLINE", which supersedes the s286 "die loud when the assumption is
violated" section (kept below it, with a pointer, for its reasoning);
docs/ir-spec.md §2.2 invariant + freeze paragraph rewritten.
subject: raw-numeric freeze DIES on an overloaded object that came from a MODULE -- FIXED s460ao by a runtime DECLINE (store the general form's own box); the <=>-only silent-wrong closed with it
